speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how frequently does NParks check its trees to ensure that they are in a healthy condition and not prone to falls; and (b) whether there is a safety check regime in place for parks under the charge of NParks to ensure that our parks remain safe for users.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the current inspection routine and procedure to ensure that trees in public areas are safe from tree rot, infestation and tree failure that can potentially cause a loss of life; (b) whether there are sufficient resources allocated to conduct these inspections; and (c) what are the scenarios that will cause a healthy tree to fail within nine months after its inspection.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Shawn Huang have raised questions about NParks’ current tree inspection regime and I will address them together.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The National Parks Board (NParks) has a tree inspection and maintenance regime that is aligned with the Best Management Practices of the International Society of Arboriculture (ISA).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Trees that are close to areas with high pedestrian or traffic activity are inspected more frequently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: During a tree inspection, NParks’ inspectors conduct a comprehensive visual examination of the tree crown, branches, trunk and roots to assess the tree’s health and stability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Trees that are found to have possible defects are subject to an additional in-depth inspection, which involves the use of diagnostic equipment to assess the internal condition of the tree.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a precautionary measure in response to changing weather conditions, and is over and above the Best Management Practices of the International Society of Arboriculture.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Beyond inspections, NParks has put in place other measures to reduce the risk of tree failure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, NParks carries out targeted arboriculture treatments to improve general tree health and their ability to withstand severe weather conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It prunes trees regularly to remove weak, dry or overgrown branches, and to improve their structure and balance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, NParks is also progressively replacing storm-vulnerable tree species with hardier species.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, NParks uses technology to analyse risks and improve inspection processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, NParks is piloting modelling techniques to understand the impact of adverse environmental conditions, such as strong winds, on the structural integrity of trees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will help NParks to better determine the pruning required to improve tree stability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To ensure that there is sufficient expertise to perform tree inspections, NParks has built up a pool of certified arborists in Singapore by offering professional training courses and seminars.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Apart from its in-house arborists, NParks also requires its tree maintenance contractors to have certified arborists in their teams.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, it is not possible to completely prevent tree-related incidents because trees are living organisms that can be affected by pests and diseases, as well as environmental conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even healthy and structurally-sound trees can fail during storm events due to exceptionally strong winds or heavy rainfall.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, Ms Hany Soh has asked whether NParks has a safety check regime in place for its parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Beyond trees, safety inspections are also carried out for park infrastructure and facilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks appoints registered professional structural engineers to inspect the structural integrity of buildings and structures in its parks, such as shelters, bridges and monuments, once every five years, in accordance with statutory requirements under the Building Control Act.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Regular and systematic checks of park facilities are also conducted by NParks staff and external inspectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, all playgrounds are inspected monthly by NParks staff, and every six months by external Certified Playground Safety Inspectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This allows NParks to detect and rectify defects in a timely manner and to keep our parks safe for users.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We deeply regret the loss of life, every one death or injury as a result of tree-fall incidents is one too many.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleagues at NParks and the arborist community work hard day after day to keep our streetscape, to keep our parks and our nature areas safe for Singaporeans to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to press on to keep up the work and to ensure that our City in Nature is safe and enjoyable for everyone.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Indeed, the victim of the recent Marsiling Park fallen tree incident is actually my Woodgrove resident.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Like the Minister, I agree with him, that every of such unfortunate incident is one too many.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another practice of tying back trees, on the other hand, as practiced by countries such as Japan, is to ensure that if trees were to fall prematurely, it will fall towards a pre-determined direction, away from human traffic.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I would like to seek the Ministry's clarification, whether they will consider implementing these measures for trees that are within parks or high human traffic areas.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My second clarification is whether NParks will consider to do more public education on safety at parks, sharing tips on how to recognise potential hazard in parks and what to do when a park-related accident occurs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On behalf of my colleagues at NParks, we extend our deepest condolences to the family of the deceased.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We stand by them and have offered the support that they may need at this difficult time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In regard to the Member's first question on the use of restraints on trees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, there is a heritage tree I am told, the Lychee Tree atop Mount Rosie in the Novena neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is supported by permanent galvanised steel structure built to withstand elements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This tree is more than 100 years old.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks also uses cabling methods in selected situations such as the tree, a Palaquium tree at the Evolution Garden at Singapore Botanic Gardens (SBG).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This method is used as a precautionary measure to restrain the tree from falling in a direction of the footpath.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This could also constrain them in their ability to make natural swaying movements in order to buffet the impact of strong winds, and in fact, may inadvertently weaken the structure of the tree – because the crown gets the full impact and the tree structure is constrained from some degree of natural movement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks will study carefully what more situations we can use it, but we also have to recognise that these structures can also pose safety issues if used without care in park settings where people frequent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To ensure that park users can enjoy our parks safely, NParks has installed advisory signs on various safety related issues across our shared spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes signs to guide the appropriate use of play and fitness equipment; as well as what the public can do when they encounter wild animals in our parks, or hazards like falling branches in forested areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks will continue to engage and educate our community on public safety tips in our parks by putting out advisories and safety messages onsite and on NParks' website.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Recognising potential tree hazards in our parks, requires assessing the health and structural integrity of trees and is best carried out by trained personnel with the requisite experience and expertise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members of the public with feedback on public trees or park facilities can contact NParks via its hotline at 1800 471 7300 or through the OneService app.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For park-related accidents or incidents, public should contact the Police or the SCDF immediately, if there is an emergency or NParks' hotline otherwise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members of the public may also approach NParks officers who are stationed onsite at some of our parks during office hours.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Besides trees in parks, many trees are actually in HDB estates managed by Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister share how does NParks work with and coordinate with the Town Councils for tree inspection and how does NParks share their expertise with the Town Councils?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They have to undergo regular training and upgrading in order to upkeep their standards and they are then certified by NParks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks offers professional training courses and seminars, both by international and local experts, and that raises and supports the standards of arborists, who are then deployed not only under NParks' regimen but also that of Town Councils, the private sector as well as other agencies as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, in relation to trees under Town Councils, NParks works closely with agencies that manage trees, Town Councils and landowners to advise them on tree care standards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks also provides professional training courses and seminars for tree care professionals in the private sector and other public agencies which manage trees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, NParks provides training for the staff of Town Councils or managing agents administering landscaping contracts, in various plant health and maintenance topics.
